resources.string: Who performs moving around the screen (navigation)
Handing over to the Android system: how it works

O‘zbegim always keeps reading the screen at full power: these choices never switch it off. If you choose “The Android system performs it”, the system itself performs double-tap and hold. When both are given to the system, dragging while holding also works (sliders, moving items); if one stays with O‘zbegim, the one given to the system is performed the way the system does it. For navigation, the order declared by the app and the system’s own focus order (Tab) are used, and moving with a physical keyboard is read aloud; if the system cannot move, O‘zbegim moves by itself. If you choose “O‘zbegim performs it”, O‘zbegim does all of this itself (recommended).

How the time is read, and instructions
13:30 can be read in two ways. Example 1: “%1$s” Example 2: “%2$s” On the exact hour only the hour is spoken: “%3$s”

1:30 in the afternoon can be read in two ways. Example 1: “%1$s” Example 2: “%2$s” Hours 1 to 12 are spoken, preceded by the part of the day (dawn, morning, daytime, evening, night). On the exact hour: “%3$s”

In example 2, minutes below 10 are spoken with a leading zero: “%1$s” The announcement is spoken in the system language; if the voice pack is in another language, it is spoken in the voice pack’s language (Uzbek, Russian or English). Current announcement language: %2$s. The same rule applies to the battery announcement.
